project_title: LottAI Phase 2 — Council of Experts + Autonomous Prediction Loop

tasks.name: Council Selection Module
tasks.description: council.py: selects 10 diverse high-performing experts from the experiment ledger using live_optimal_ev as the score and model_fingerprint diversity as a constraint. Persists council.json.
acceptance_criteria: council.py --rebuild reads experiments_v4.jsonl + live_eval_results_v2.jsonl and writes council.json with exactly 10 entries
No two council members share the same model_fingerprint (sorted tuple of model types)
All selected members have a live_optimal_ev score (have been live-evaluated)
council.json contains for each member: exp_num, config dict, live_optimal_ev, val_optimal_ev, model_fingerprint, pipeline_fingerprint, date_admitted
council.py --show prints current council sorted by live_optimal_ev
council.py --validate confirms all 10 configs pass config_validator.validate_config()

subtasks.name: Define council.json schema and load/save helpers
Implement model_fingerprint and pipeline_fingerprint derivation from config
Implement greedy diversity-aware selection: score by live_ev, reject fingerprint duplicates
Add --rebuild, --show, --validate CLI flags via argparse
Write tests/test_council_selection.py covering diversity constraint, min live-eval requirement, schema validation

reference_patterns: autoresearch/live_eval_v2.py -- live_eval_results_v2.jsonl schema and loading pattern
hints.notes: model_fingerprint = tuple(sorted(m['type'] for m in config['models'])). pipeline_fingerprint = tuple(s['stage'] for s in config.get('pipeline', [])). Greedy selection: iterate live_ev descending, add to council if model_fingerprint not already represented. council.json is git-tracked (it is derived metadata, not raw live data).

tasks.name: Prediction Engine
tasks.description: predictor.py: retrains all council models on data through the most recent draw, collects per-digit probability vectors, computes weighted ensemble, finds optimal-K ticket recommendation.
acceptance_criteria: predictor.py --council council.json outputs a ranked 1000-combo probability matrix
Each council member's models are trained on rows 0 through (last live draw index)
Ensemble weights are softmax-normalized live_optimal_ev scores
Optimal K is computed as argmax_k(top_k_hit_rate * 500 - k) over k=1..20
Output JSON contains: top_k, expected_ev, predictions list [{combo, probability}] sorted descending
Runs in under 60 minutes for 10 council members on beastmode hardware
Prediction uses only training+live data features; live outcomes are never passed to any LLM

subtasks.name: Extend template_engine.py or create a prediction-mode render that captures clf objects and predict_proba output instead of val score
Build 'next draw' feature vector using prepare_v3.build_features on last live row index
Implement weighted ensemble: softmax weights, averaged P(d1/d2/d3) vectors across members
Compute 1000-combo probability matrix and find optimal K via EV formula
Output prediction JSON to stdout and/or file
Write tests/test_predictor.py with mock council (known priors, verify correct weighted average)

reference_patterns: autoresearch/live_eval_v2.py -- how live rows are appended to full_df for feature building
autoresearch/runner_v4.py -- how experiment code is executed and results extracted
hints.notes: The cleanest approach is a new template render mode (e.g. live_eval=False, predict_mode=True) that trains on train+val+test+live rows and then calls clf.predict_proba([[X_next]]) for each digit. The next draw feature context is row index = len(full_df) + len(live_df), which means we build features for a hypothetical row whose 'previous draw' is the last live draw. Softmax weights: w_i = exp(live_ev_i) / sum(exp(live_ev_j)).

tasks.name: Live Data Updater
tasks.description: live_update.py: downloads the four Texas Lottery CSV files, filters to rows after the training cutoff (2026-02-13), appends only new rows to the *_live.csv files, rebuilds pick3all_live.csv.
acceptance_criteria: live_update.py downloads all four draw-time CSVs from Texas Lottery URLs
Only rows with draw date > last known date in each live file are appended (no duplicates)
pick3all_live.csv is rebuilt from the four updated individual files
Returns count of new rows added per draw time
Handles network failure gracefully: logs error, leaves existing files unchanged
Runs in under 30 seconds under normal network conditions

subtasks.name: Implement download_csv(url) with retry logic (3 attempts, 5s backoff)
Implement append_new_rows(downloaded_df, live_path, cutoff_date) that appends only rows after last known date
Implement rebuild_combined(four_live_paths, combined_path) sorted by date
Add --dry-run flag that reports new row counts without writing

reference_patterns: BRIEFING.md -- Texas Lottery CSV download URLs
autoresearch/live_eval_v2.py _build_combined_live() -- existing combine logic to reuse
hints.notes: Download URLs are in BRIEFING.md. The existing live_eval_v2.py already has _build_combined_live() -- extract it into live_update.py as the canonical implementation and import it back in live_eval_v2.py to avoid duplication. tasks.name: Prediction Ledger
tasks.description: prediction_ledger.py: writes one JSONL record per prediction before the draw, then fills in actual_combo/hit/hit_at_k after draw results are available. Provides running statistics for the whitepaper.
acceptance_criteria: write_prediction(prediction_id, draw_slot, predicted_draw_date, predictions, council_meta) appends a record to prediction_ledger.jsonl
update_outcome(prediction_id, actual_combo) fills in actual_combo, hit (bool), hit_at_k (int or null) for the matching record
hit_at_k is the smallest K such that actual_combo appears in top-K predictions, or null if not in top-20
get_statistics() returns hit rate at K=1,5,10,16,20, mean EV vs random baseline, count by draw_slot
prediction_ledger.py --stats prints current statistics to stdout
Records are append-only; update_outcome rewrites only the matching line

subtasks.name: Define prediction record schema as a dataclass or TypedDict
Implement write_prediction() that appends to prediction_ledger.jsonl
Implement update_outcome() that rewrites the matching line with actual result
Implement get_statistics() with hit rate at K breakpoints and EV comparison
Add --stats and --update flags to CLI
Write tests/test_prediction_ledger.py (write, update, stats calculation)

hints.notes: update_outcome reads all lines, finds matching prediction_id, updates the dict, rewrites the file. This is safe at <10K records. prediction_id format: '{YYYY-MM-DD}T{HH:MM:SS}_{draw_slot}' e.g. '2026-04-26T10:27:00_morning'. hit_at_k: iterate sorted predictions, find first K where actual_combo appears in combos[0:K]. Random baseline EV = 500 * 0.001 - 1 = -0.50.

tasks.name: Analysis Generator
tasks.description: analysis.py: produces a 150-300 word writeup for each prediction using a local LLM (Ollama/MiniMax). Input is prediction metadata and council composition only — no raw live draw data is passed to the LLM.
acceptance_criteria: generate_analysis(prediction_result, council_meta) returns a string of 150-300 words
Input to LLM contains: top-K combos, per-digit confidence spread, council size and top live EV, but NOT raw live draw history
Falls back to a template-generated summary if LLM is unreachable
Output is suitable for direct inclusion in Telegram message
generate_analysis completes in under 60 seconds

subtasks.name: Define LLM prompt template that summarizes prediction without exposing live data
Implement Ollama API call (POST /api/generate) with timeout and retry
Implement template fallback for LLM unavailability
Write tests/test_analysis.py with mock Ollama response and fallback path

reference_patterns: autoresearch/runner_v4.py -- existing Ollama API call pattern (POST /api/chat)
hints.notes: The LLM prompt should describe the prediction in terms of signal strength (e.g. 'the d1 model shows 47% confidence on digit 5, well above the 10% uniform baseline') rather than raw data rows. Use minimax-m2.7:cloud via Ollama. Live data boundary: never include actual draw outcomes, live CSV data, or live_optimal_ev comparisons in the LLM prompt -- only the current prediction output.

tasks.name: Telegram Notifier
tasks.description: telegram_bot.py: formats the prediction output and analysis writeup into a Telegram message and sends it via the Bot API to the configured chat. Handles send failures gracefully.
acceptance_criteria: send_prediction(prediction_result, analysis_text) sends a formatted message to TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID
Message includes: draw slot + date, top-K combo list formatted as NNN, buy count, expected EV, analysis text
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID are read from environment variables (never hardcoded)
Send failure logs the error and returns False without raising
Message length stays under Telegram's 4096 character limit; truncates analysis if needed
send_prediction completes in under 10 seconds under normal network conditions

subtasks.name: Implement format_message(prediction_result, analysis_text) returning a string under 4096 chars
Implement send_telegram(message, bot_token, chat_id) using requests POST to Bot API sendMessage endpoint

Write tests/test_telegram_bot.py with mock requests response (success + failure)

reference_patterns: autoresearch/runner_v4.py -- environment variable loading pattern (.env via dotenv or os.environ)
hints.notes: Telegram Bot API endpoint: https://api.telegram.org/bot{TOKEN}/sendMessage with JSON body {chat_id, text, parse_mode='Markdown'}. Combo format: bold the combo string e.g. *123*. Message template: header line, blank line, numbered combo list with probability, blank line, buy/EV summary, blank line, analysis. No external dependencies beyond requests (already in requirements.txt).

tasks.name: GA Discovery Runner
tasks.description: ga_discovery.py: launches a fixed-size batch of GA/random experiments (default 10) as a background subprocess using runner_v4.py. Does not block the prediction pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: ga_discovery.py --n 10 launches runner_v4.py --resume --max (current_count+10) as a subprocess
Process runs in background; ga_discovery.py returns immediately after launch
Subprocess inherits the venv and working directory correctly
Subprocess stdout/stderr appended to autoresearch_v4.log
ga_discovery.py --wait blocks until subprocess completes (used in testing)
ga_discovery.py --status reports whether a discovery subprocess is currently running

subtasks.name: Determine current experiment count from experiments_v4.jsonl and compute --max target
Launch runner_v4.py as subprocess.Popen with stdout/stderr appended to log
Write PID to .discovery.pid file so --status can check if still running
Add --n, --wait, --status CLI flags
Write tests/test_ga_discovery.py with mock subprocess (verify correct --max is computed)

hints.notes: Current experiment count: sum(1 for line in open('experiments_v4.jsonl') if line.strip()). Launch: subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, 'runner_v4.py', '--resume', '--max', str(target), '--random-frac', '0.25'], stdout=log_fh, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT). Store pid in .discovery.pid; check os.kill(pid, 0) for --status. .discovery.pid should be gitignored.

tasks.name: Model Promotion Checker
tasks.description: promotion_checker.py: after each GA discovery batch, identifies new experiments that could displace council members, runs live_eval on candidates, and updates council.json if a better member is found.
acceptance_criteria: promotion_checker.py reads council.json to get council floor (weakest member's live_optimal_ev) and last_checked_exp
Candidate filter: new experiments (exp_num > last_checked_exp) with val_optimal_ev > council floor
Runs live_eval_v2.py --jsonl experiments_v4.jsonl --ids <candidates> on filtered set
If any candidate's live_ev > council floor AND its model_fingerprint is not already in council: replace weakest member
If candidate has same fingerprint as existing member but higher live_ev: replace that member
All promotions appended to council_history.jsonl with old_member, new_member, live_ev_delta, timestamp
council.json updated_at timestamp updated after any changes
council.py --show reflects new composition after promotion

subtasks.name: Implement get_candidates(council, experiments_jsonl) returning exp_nums to evaluate
Implement run_live_eval_on_candidates(exp_nums) calling live_eval_v2.py subprocess
Implement promotion decision: diversity-aware replacement logic
Implement council_history.jsonl append for each promotion event
Write tests/test_promotion_checker.py with synthetic experiments and council state

reference_patterns: autoresearch/live_eval_v2.py -- --ids flag added in current session
hints.notes: council floor = min(m['live_optimal_ev'] for m in council['members']). last_checked_exp stored in council.json and updated after each check. Diversity-aware replacement: if candidate fingerprint already in council, only replace the existing member with that fingerprint if candidate live_ev is strictly higher. Promotion is conservative -- only promote if clearly better, not just marginally.

tasks.name: Orchestrator
tasks.description: orchestrator.py: the main cron entry point. Runs Track A (update data → predict → notify → log) synchronously, then launches Track B (GA discovery → promotion check) in background.
acceptance_criteria: orchestrator.py runs Track A end-to-end and exits 0 on success
Any Track A step failure logs the error and continues to the next step where possible (prediction failure still runs GA)
Track B (ga_discovery + promotion_checker) is launched as background subprocess before orchestrator exits
Total Track A wall time logged to orchestrator.log
orchestrator.py --dry-run runs Track A but skips Telegram send and prediction ledger write
orchestrator.py --skip-discovery skips Track B entirely
All steps log to autoresearch/orchestrator.log with timestamps

subtasks.name: Implement Track A sequence: live_update → predictor → analysis → telegram → ledger
Add per-step error handling: catch, log, continue where safe
Launch Track B as background subprocess (ga_discovery --n 10 && promotion_checker)
Add --dry-run and --skip-discovery flags
Write tests/test_orchestrator.py with all steps mocked, verifying call order and error isolation

hints.notes: Track A is synchronous and must complete before the next draw (~2 hours). Track B runs async and may complete in the background. If live_update returns 0 new draws (draw hasn't posted yet), orchestrator should log and exit gracefully without running prediction -- the prediction context would be stale. draw_slot and predicted_draw_date derived from current datetime + schedule knowledge.

tasks.name: Docker and Cron Setup
tasks.description: Dockerfile, docker-compose.yaml, and crontab for the OpenBrain container. Mounts the LottAI data directory, sets correct timezone for Texas draw schedule, loads .env credentials.
acceptance_criteria: docker-compose up builds and starts the container without errors
Container has access to /mnt/beastmode/lottai via a bind mount
Cron fires orchestrator.py at the four Texas Lottery draw times (Mon-Sat, Central Time)
All Python dependencies from requirements.txt are installed in the container
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID, OLLAMA_HOST, and LOTTAI_ROOT are injected from .env
.env is gitignored; .env.example documents all required variables
Container logs cron output to a mounted log file visible on the host

reference_patterns: BRIEFING.md -- draw times: Morning 10am, Day 12:27pm, Evening 6pm, Night 10:12pm Central
hints.notes: Cron draw-time entries (Central, which is UTC-5 standard / UTC-6 daylight -- use TZ env var and let cron handle it): '27 10 * * 1-6', '57 12 * * 1-6', '30 18 * * 1-6', '42 22 * * 1-6'. The container needs GPU passthrough if xgb_gpu/lgb_gpu models are in the council -- add 'deploy: resources: reservations: devices' in compose. Ollama is on the host; OLLAMA_HOST should use host.docker.internal or the host's LAN IP.
